name: Meiyu Front Lingers
description: The Meiyu front stalls over Taiwan, bringing extended rainfall that boosts northern and central reservoirs.
news_on_start: The Meiyu front is lingering over Taiwan; meteorologists warn of potential heavy rain.
Water Resources Agency: Moisture from the Meiyu front should replenish northern reservoirs.
news_on_end: The Meiyu front shifts northward and rainfall gradually eases.

name: Pacific High Pressure Dominates
description: Persistent high pressure brings hot, dry weather and makes typhoon formation more difficult.
news_on_start: Pacific high pressure strengthens, turning Taiwan hot and dry.
Agricultural agencies warn: Irrigation demand is rising, carefully manage water supplies.
news_on_end: The Pacific high weakens and afternoon convection slowly returns.

name: Autumn Typhoon Surge
description: Warm western Pacific waters may bring successive autumn typhoons to Taiwan.
news_on_start: Weather center notes: Elevated autumn sea temperatures could intensify developing typhoons.
Local governments mobilize: Autumn typhoon preparedness drills are underway.
news_on_end: Autumn typhoon formation tapers off as ocean heat wanes.

name: Northeast Monsoon Strengthens
description: The northeast monsoon pushes cool, damp air southward, bringing prolonged rain to northern and eastern Taiwan.
news_on_start: The northeast monsoon arrives and wind and rain pick up along the north coast.
Transport ministry cautions: Mountain roads face increased risk of falling rocks and landslides.
news_on_end: The northeast monsoon weakens and the weather gradually stabilizes.

name: Election Sensitivity Period
description: Public sentiment is highly sensitive before elections, and every closure or disaster report receives intense scrutiny.
news_on_start: With elections approaching, local leaders demand precise forecasts from the weather deity.
Polling shows the public is closely watching decisions on typhoon-day closures.
news_on_end: The election concludes and the public mood returns to normal.
